title: JC H2 biology — cell: ultrastructure and biomolecules
subject: science
strengths: Most of the class can describe the fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane.
The class can trace a protein from the rough ER through the Golgi apparatus to export.

modelAnswers.question: A leaf cell contains both chloroplasts and mitochondria. Explain, in terms of photosynthesis and respiration, why it needs both.
modelAnswers.answer: Chloroplasts trap light energy to make sugar in photosynthesis; mitochondria release energy from that sugar as ATP in aerobic respiration, which continues day and night.
creditPoints: The two organelles do different jobs: grana and stroma in the chloroplast build sugar (scene s4), cristae in the mitochondrion release its energy (scene s3)
Carries the working through to the correct final answer

modelAnswers.question: Describe the structure of the cell membrane in the fluid mosaic model and explain how that structure makes it selectively permeable.
modelAnswers.answer: A phospholipid bilayer with hydrophilic heads facing outward and hydrophobic tails inside, with proteins drifting through it; channel proteins allow only selected substances to cross.
creditPoints: Scene s1 shows heads facing water, tails hidden inside, and a channel protein spanning the membrane: small selected substances pass through channels while others are kept out
Carries the working through to the correct final answer

commonErrors.example: A learner claims a leaf cell needs no mitochondria because its chloroplasts supply all its energy.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: state what chloroplasts do with light energy and what mitochondria do with the sugar that is made, including at night.
fixIt.corrected: Chloroplasts trap light energy to make sugar in photosynthesis; mitochondria respire that sugar to release ATP day and night, so a leaf cell needs both organelles.

commonErrors.example: On the worksheet, a learner says root hair cells cannot respire because they have no chloroplasts.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: name the organelle that releases energy in a root hair cell and the process it carries out.
fixIt.corrected: A root hair cell respires glucose in its mitochondria to release ATP; plant cells contain mitochondria whether or not they photosynthesise.

nextSteps: Reteach the division of labour between chloroplasts and mitochondria, including night-time respiration.
Practise pairing each organelle with its process and its product before the next quiz.
